content:
Welcome back to Step By Step Reviewed, the only blog on the internet that has watched 151 episodes of Step By Step on purpose. Today is episode 152. There are eight left. I can see the light at the end of the tunnel and it is beige.

Quick reminder of where we are in the SBSCU timeline: Step By Step is on **CBS** now. ABC looked at six years of Lamberts and Fosters, said "we're good," and left the whole family on the curb with a FREE sign taped to it, like a couch. CBS took the couch. CBS always takes the couch.

## The Premise, Which I Promise I Am Not Making Up

![s7e11-open.jpg](stepbystepreviewed/s7e11-open.jpg)

Here is the official plot of this episode, straight from the episode guides: Al gets hired to star in a commercial for suntan lotion. The commercial turns out to be for a **phone sex hotline.**

That's real. A family sitcom built 22 minutes around a 1-900 number. I have accused this show of a lot of things over 151 episodes, but I have never accused it of being horny on purpose. Frank is horny, sure, but that's a character trait, not a premise. This is the first time the *whole episode* got horny. New network, new vibe. Welcome to Season 7.

Al, for any newcomers (there are no newcomers; nobody starts a blog series at episode 152), started this show as the tomboy daughter who assaulted Karen with a ketchup bottle in the pilot. Seven seasons later, the show has decided she can book a suntan lotion commercial. Character development! [CHECK: how the show plays Al by Season 7; adjust if she is no longer the tomboy at all.]

## Nobody Reads Anything, Ever

![s7e11-hired.jpg](stepbystepreviewed/s7e11-hired.jpg)

Let's take stock of the adults in this house. Frank is a contractor. He signs contracts for a living. It's in the name. Carol owns a beauty salon. She runs a business. Between the two of them they have roughly forty years of experience reading the fine print.

Nobody reads the fine print. Nobody asks to see a script. Nobody asks what the lotion is called, who makes it, or why the "producer" works out of whatever room he works out of. [CHECK: where the producer works and what he looks like; this is the setup for every joke below, so give him one real detail.] A teenage girl gets offered money to be on TV and the entire GM-BTU parenting apparatus goes "neat."

This is not a knock on Al. Al is a kid. Kids should not read contracts. That's why kids have parents. Frank and Carol are parents in the sense that they are taller than the children and own the house.

## The Shoot: A Masterclass in Efficiency

![s7e11-shoot.jpg](stepbystepreviewed/s7e11-shoot.jpg)

Here's what I want to know, and I want you to sit with it for a second like I had to: **what footage works for both of these products?**

Think about it. The producer filmed one commercial. Then he sold it to two industries. Suntan lotion and phone sex. The same footage. Whatever Al did on that set was *exactly* sunscreen enough and *exactly* 1-900 enough at the same time. That is a very narrow target and this sleazebag hit it dead center.

I'm going to be honest with you. This is the most efficient thing anyone has done in seven seasons of this show. Frank's construction company could learn something from this man. Frank cannot make a burger. This guy made one commercial into two revenue streams. [CHECK: what Al actually does or says in the shoot, and which line or shot ends up in the hotline ad. Quote it here. The joke lands harder with the real line.]

## Family Television Night

![s7e11-tv.jpg](stepbystepreviewed/s7e11-tv.jpg)

So the family sees the ad on TV, and they are **confused.** That's the official word from the episode guide. Not horrified. Not furious. Confused.

First question: who in this house was up watching the kind of TV that runs phone sex ads? Those commercials do not run during the CBS Friday lineup. Somebody in the Lambert-Foster compound was watching late-night cable on purpose, and I think we need to talk about who. My money is on Frank. My second guess is Mark, who has been suspiciously quiet since he put his balls on the kitchen table in the pilot. [CHECK: who is in the room when the ad airs, and when.]

Second question, and this is the big one: **Suzanne Somers is confused by a late-night TV ad.**

Suzanne Somers. The ThighMaster lady. A woman who made a fortune off of late-night television ads selling America a device you squeeze between your thighs. She is standing in her living room, baffled that somebody would use late-night TV to sell something involving thighs. Carol, buddy. You *invented* this. You're in this picture and you don't like it.

Then Al has to explain to her own family what they just watched. A teenager stands in the middle of the living room and walks two grown adults through the business model of the 1-900 industry. This is the most honest scene in Step By Step history, and it's about phone sex. Seven seasons of hugging and learning and the one thing this family ever really learns, out loud, together, is how phone sex lines work.

## JT, Hired Muscle

![s7e11-jt.jpg](stepbystepreviewed/s7e11-jt.jpg)

Al decides she needs backup to go confront the sneaky producer. Let's look at her options. Frank: grown man, owns a truck full of hammers. Carol: grown woman, owns a business, could presumably call a lawyer. Dana: the smart one, could presumably *be* a lawyer by now.

She picks JT.

And you know what? I hate this, but it's the right call. When you need somebody to do something morally gray to a sleazy adult, you don't call the guy who reads contracts. You call the guy with a body count. JT put a live rat in Dana's locker and let it die, in the *pilot*, and has never once been asked to account for it. That man has been waiting 151 episodes for a job like this.

JT's career so far:

- **Rats murdered:** 1
- **Sleazy producers confronted:** 1
- **Homework completed:** [CHECK: running joke from earlier posts]

[CHECK: how the confrontation goes. Two drafts below; keep the one that matches the episode and delete the other.]

**If JT wins by being scary:** The producer folds the second JT walks in, which tells you two things. One, this guy is a coward. Two, the writers looked at seven seasons of JT, thought "what's his skill," and landed on "looming." They're not wrong. JT looms like a pro.

**If JT blows it and Al saves herself:** Of course JT blows it. JT has never successfully done anything in this show except kill a rodent. Al has to clean up the mess herself, which is the actual lesson of every episode of Step By Step: if you want something done, do not bring a Lambert. Unless you are a Lambert. Then I don't know what to tell you.

## The Hug

![s7e11-hug.jpg](stepbystepreviewed/s7e11-hug.jpg)

I'm not going to describe it. You know what happens. Somebody says something about family, the soft music comes in, the audience goes "aww," and everyone hugs about phone sex. [CHECK: confirm there is a hug. If there isn't one, that's a much bigger story and gets its own section.]

## Running Tallies

- **Episodes left:** 8
- **Characters Patrika Darbo'd so far:** [CHECK: carry the count from the last post]
- **Times anyone in this family read a contract:** 0
- **Phone sex hotlines in the GM-BTU:** 1. As far as I know, Full House never did one. Danny Tanner would have disinfected the phone.

## The Brady Bunch Test

The Brady kids once got hired for a commercial too. [CHECK: the Brady Bunch episode where the kids shoot a detergent commercial; confirm the title and product before posting.] Their commercial was for laundry soap. Nobody's commercial turned out to be for anything else, because the Bradys lived in a world with standards.

**0% Brady.** First zero of the season.

## Lesson of the Week

Read the contract. Or, if you're a Lambert, have JT read it to you, slowly, out loud, while he points at the parts he doesn't like.

Eight left.
